en.title: Quantifiers: some, many, few
en.summary: Quantifiers such as some, many and few tell us how much or how many.

paragraphs: Quantifiers tell us how much or how many there is of something. They stand before a noun. Some go with countable nouns, some with uncountable nouns, and some with both. They are one of the groups of determiners.

Use many, few and a few with countable nouns, and much, little and a little with uncountable ones. Some, any, a lot of and no go with both. Few and little mean almost none and are negative. A few and a little mean some and are positive.

blocks.html:
CountableUncountable
many booksmuch time
few books (almost none)little time (almost none)
a few books (some)a little time (some)
a lot of booksa lot of time
some bookssome time

paragraphs: Some is normal in positive sentences, and any in negatives and questions: I have some money, I don't have any money, Do you have any money? We use some in offers and requests: Would you like some tea?
In positive statements, much and many sound formal. People say a lot of: We have a lot of time. Much and many are common in negatives and questions: How much does it cost?

items: Wrong: **I have few time.** Right: **I have little time.**
Wrong: **many water** Right: **a lot of water** or **much water**
Wrong: **I don't have some money.** Right: **I don't have any money.**

ro.title: Cuantificatorii: unii, mulți, puțini
ro.summary: Cuantificatorii arată cantitatea și își schimbă forma după genul și numărul substantivului.

paragraphs: Cuantificatorii arată cantitatea sau numărul unor lucruri. Ei exprimă o cantitate aproximativă. Folosim aceste cuvinte direct în fața substantivelor.
La singular, folosim cuantificatorii pentru lucruri care nu se numără. La plural, îi folosim pentru lucruri pe care le numărăm. Formele se schimbă după gen și număr.
